body.problem: Every stage of the insrc workflow ends in a document a human must read, understand, and approve before the next stage may proceed — yet the documents the framework produces are shaped for machine and developer consumption rather than for the people who have to review them. They are dense and structurally uniform in a way that is hard for any reader to navigate, and they are geared almost entirely toward implementation detail even though the earliest artifacts are the ones most likely to be reviewed by non-technical business and product stakeholders who need to see the functional intent — what is being built and why, in outcome terms — rather than its construction. That functional intent is captured only thinly and is not carried as a durable, checkable thread through the later stages, so there is no reliable way to confirm at the end that what was built actually realizes what was originally asked for. Content compounds the difficulty: the same material is repeated verbatim across documents (for example a design's summary copied into every lower-level design derived from it), inflating each document and burying the part that is actually specific to it. Where a design decision, a flow, a data shape, or a user-facing surface would be far clearer shown visually, the documents offer only prose, and the user-experience design that the recent chat-UI work showed is decisive to getting a feature right is not connected to the generated documents at all — a reviewer cannot see the intended experience or the mock it should match while reading the design that is supposed to honour it. Finally, none of these qualities is something the workflow can require or verify: readability, functional completeness, the presence of a useful diagram where one is warranted, and adherence to an agreed experience are left to chance at exactly the human-in-the-loop gates the workflow most depends on, so a document can pass review while being hard to read, functionally vague, redundant, and disconnected from the experience it designs.

nonGoals.text: Reformatting or migrating the artifact documents that already exist on disk into any new structure.
nonGoals.rationale: The improvement is forward-only by explicit stakeholder decision (c2) — it applies to documents generated after the change; retrofitting historical artifacts is out of scope and risks churn against records that are already approved and correlated.

nonGoals.text: Changing the on-disk folder layout, canonical identity, or naming of artifacts.
nonGoals.rationale: That concern was already addressed by the separate `restructure-docs-artifact-markdown-from-flat` Epic (c6); this Epic is about the content and readability of the documents, not where they are filed.

nonGoals.text: Replacing the core artifact format with a non-markdown medium (HTML/PDF/rich docs) for the primary document body.
nonGoals.rationale: Stakeholder decision (c2) is that the core documents stay well-structured markdown; only companion visual artifacts may be other media, referenced from the markdown.

nonGoals.text: Making design diagrams a mandatory element of every document.
nonGoals.rationale: Stakeholder decision (c2): diagrams are included only where the document flow assesses one is genuinely useful; forcing a diagram onto every document would add noise, not readability.

nonGoals.text: Introducing any direct cloud REST provider for diagram/content generation.
nonGoals.rationale: Project principle (c7) forbids direct cloud REST from our process; all LLM/diagram generation must go through the existing local CliProvider/Ollama and docgen seams.

assumptions.text: The functional intent can be represented as structured data in the artifact JSON with the human-readable prose generated from it, so the prose and the structured record cannot drift apart.
A blocking completion gate already exists that new adherence checks (functional-coverage, diagram, UX) can ride rather than inventing a separate enforcement mechanism.
The existing per-type markdown renderers, the synthesizer, the approval/validation gates, the path-scheme, and the template loader are the seams this work modifies, and all of them already exist.
Design-diagram generation can reuse the existing docgen capability rather than building diagram generation from scratch.
Verbatim content duplication across documents (e.g. an upper design's summary copied into every lower design) is present today and is a material driver of the readability problem.

constraints.text: The core document body of every artifact type must remain well-structured markdown; any visual (UML/Mermaid or UX/HTML) is a separate companion artifact referenced from the markdown, never inlined into the core body.

The functional-definition record is structured data in the artifact JSON and is the single source of truth; the document prose is generated from it (no functional requirement is authored in prose alone).
Diagram inclusion is content-gated — the document flow must assess per-document whether a diagram is genuinely useful and only then generate one; diagrams are never mandatory.
New adherence checks (functional-coverage, diagram, UX) are enforced by riding the existing blocking code-review completion gate, not a new parallel gate.
All content and diagram generation goes through the local CliProvider/Ollama and the existing docgen seams — no direct cloud REST from our process.
The change is forward-only: it applies to newly generated artifacts and does not migrate or rewrite artifacts already on disk.

stories.title: Carry a functional-definition thread from the first document through to completion
stories.userValue: A reviewer — including a non-technical business or product stakeholder — can see what is being built and why in outcome terms, and at the end the team can confirm the implementation actually realizes what was asked for.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a new piece of work enters the workflow
acceptanceCriteria.then: the document states its functional requirements as discrete, individually-identified outcomes — each carrying a stable identifier — that a non-technical reviewer can read and approve

acceptanceCriteria.given: functional requirements are established in an upstream document
acceptanceCriteria.when: a downstream document derived from it is generated
acceptanceCriteria.then: it carries those same identified requirements forward unchanged in identity, so the functional thread is continuous and traceable across every stage

acceptanceCriteria.given: the functional requirements for a piece of work and its completed build
acceptanceCriteria.then: the workflow judges whether each functional requirement was genuinely realized and withholds completion when that coverage is inadequate, using the existing blocking completion gate

localConstraints.text: Functional-requirement identifiers use the same sequence-based numbering used for tasks and stories, of the form `<epicId>:FRxxx`, and are stable once assigned.

stories.title: Make each document human-readable and audience-aware, without repeated content
stories.userValue: Any reviewer can navigate a document quickly and read only the parts specific to it; business and product reviewers get a framing document geared to them; and no document is padded with material copied verbatim from another.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a document of any workflow type is generated
acceptanceCriteria.then: it presents a consistent, navigable structure appropriate to its type — an overview/contents, a summary, a problem statement, references, and clearly delineated per-item sections — shaped for human reading

acceptanceCriteria.given: an upstream document already states context shared with the documents derived from it
acceptanceCriteria.then: the later document references that shared context rather than reproducing it verbatim, so each document foregrounds what is specific to it

acceptanceCriteria.given: the earliest framing document is generated
acceptanceCriteria.when: a non-technical business or product reviewer reads it
acceptanceCriteria.then: its content is expressed in functional and outcome terms suited to that audience rather than in implementation detail

stories.title: Include a design diagram only where a visual genuinely aids understanding
stories.userValue: A reviewer sees a diagram exactly when a flow, structure, or data shape is clearer shown than described, is not made to wade through diagrams that add nothing, and can trust that any diagram shown matches the design it depicts.

acceptanceCriteria.when: the flow assesses whether a visual would materially aid understanding of the document's content
acceptanceCriteria.then: it includes a referenced diagram only when one is genuinely useful and omits any diagram otherwise

acceptanceCriteria.given: a diagram is warranted for a document
acceptanceCriteria.then: it is a separate companion artifact referenced from the core markdown body, never inlined into that body

acceptanceCriteria.when: the work is assessed for completion
acceptanceCriteria.then: the workflow checks that the referenced diagram is present and consistent with the design it depicts and withholds completion on a mismatch via the existing blocking gate
it uses only the local and existing generation capabilities with no direct cloud REST call from our process

stories.title: Carry the intended user experience into the design and enforce adherence to it
stories.userValue: When a feature has a user-facing surface, a reviewer can see the intended experience and the mock it must match while reading the design, and the feature cannot be completed until the built experience adheres to that agreed design.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a piece of work has a user-facing experience
acceptanceCriteria.then: the document references the agreed experience design (its mock) and describes the intended experience, so a reviewer can assess the design against what the user will actually see

acceptanceCriteria.given: a work item is flagged as having a user-facing experience
acceptanceCriteria.then: a user-experience acceptance check is required and a failing check withholds completion via the existing blocking gate

acceptanceCriteria.when: they are recorded for a work item
acceptanceCriteria.then: they are expressed as an explicit, selectable set of adherence dimensions — for example user experience, the relevant diagram kinds, and functional-requirement coverage — that the completion check reads and enforces

citations.quotedText: the generated MD files are still very machine optimized and hence hard for a person to review, both in format and content; the current docs capture very little functional definition ... functional definitions need to flow thru the workflow

Approved brainstorm SpecArtifact: one Epic, four forward-only Stories A→B→C→D; core documents stay well-structured MD, diagrams are referenced companion artifacts, FR source of truth is the JSON with prose generated from it, diagrams as-required (content-gated).
renderLldMarkdown — the largest per-type renderer (227 lines); HLD-context content is duplicated verbatim into every LLD.
codeReview.enforce boolean default false — enforce a blocking code-review verdict at Story completion (off ⇒ advisory).

Per-type renderers under artifacts/ (define.ts:86, hld.ts:105, lld.ts:282, plan.ts:97); gate approveArtifactByJsonPath in gates.ts; validateArtifact in code-review/runner.ts:266; resolveArtifactMdPath in path-scheme.ts; loadTemplate in daemon/artifacts/template-loader.ts:156. Every touched seam already exists.
Reorganized artifact folder structure + canonical identity/naming — not document content or readability.
No direct cloud REST calls from our process. Cloud LLM access happens through the locally-installed claude and codex CLI binaries (via CliProvider).
docgen registry generates self-contained HTML/Mermaid docs from the code graph — reusable diagram-generation seam.

The mock (k5) was the source of truth but never an acceptance criterion ... UX design needs to be deeply integrated into the generated documents — the reason UX adherence must be a first-class, enforced dimension.
